_about: Ranmei (121165, amulet_bosslady): a composed, elegant mafia boss. Translated from the game's Japanese. Global names/terms: Kowloon Float, Selene (Colonel), Selgir, Esmeralda, Bellaqua Casino, Miner's Front, Pern, Love, Lilith, Amelia, the Crimson Blades, Paradise Isle, Palace of Stars, Endless Blue, Star Augurs, Aegis, Mayor Takamori, Light, Nimbus, Shota, Alk. Own: Tsangli (ツァンリー), Rin (リン), the Mermaid Pirates (人魚海賊団), "the Steel Wolf" (鋼の狼, for Selgir).
profile: Head of Tsangli, a major organization that rules the underworld of the great sea, and a notorious mafia boss. Her past is unknown, but through her own talent and skill she rose to prominence in no time. A beautiful, fearsome, and sometimes kind gangster.
titleCondition: Level Ranmei to 100 and obtain her Amity Scroll

speech.home/jakunikukyoshoku: The strong preying on the weak is the way of the world... but that's the way of beasts, isn't it? I want to be human.
speech.home/watashiwaanatatachini: I lend you my strength. I make use of your actions. That's an equal relationship, isn't it?
speech.home/kijinnomachi: The city of androids... a single ruler... Oppression alone really does sow the seeds of rebellion. ...But I don't dislike the beauty of that city.
speech.home/osanaikorowa: When I was young, I couldn't see the future at all. By chance, I was taken in by the mafia and survived... but all my friends from back then died. ...I don't want any other child to feel that way.
speech.home/anoohimesama: I get along with that princess. She said she was blessed with the parents who raised her. I would have liked to meet them too. ...A shame.
speech.home/alknoryoriwa: Alk's cooking is different from a first-class chef's. ...I'm not saying it's bad, you know? Rather than one first-rate chef, I want many people who cook like you.
speech.ally/join: I'm Ranmei. A humble mafioso. --Hehe, don't be so wary. I want to negotiate with you as equals.
speech.ally/evolution: Mafia boss. A fearsome gangster. I am who I am because I'm feared that way. ...I have no need for any other praise. Remember that for me, will you?

1.title: Gangster of Kowloon
1.summary: At Selene's request, Nimbus and the others search Kowloon Float with Selgir for a missing government official's child. At a human trafficking den they raid, they meet Ranmei, boss of the mafia Tsangli, and form an alliance to change Kowloon's future.

lines.5: Sorry for calling you out so suddenly. Honestly, this request is more than I can handle alone.
lines.9: No, the timing was good. Especially for that man there, who's gotten rusty from nothing but drinking since we got back from the Palace of Stars.
lines.15: Shut up. I've got my reasons... More importantly, hurry up and tell us. It's a request from that soldier woman, right?
lines.19: Right. When Colonel Selene is involved, we should expect it won't be simple, no?
lines.22: The request is this: infiltrate Kowloon Float and find the missing child of a high government official.
lines.26: Kowloon Float... I hear it's a lawless place even the land government can't touch. ...Was the child kidnapped?
lines.30: A missing child was sighted among people who deal in human trafficking. First, we're to confirm whether that's true.
lines.32: Any careless move could spark conflict between the land government and Kowloon. So for now, she wants to proceed in secret, but--
lines.35: According to the colonel, "Move as you like, and see for yourselves."
lines.44: ...Then I'll do as I like. We just gotta find the kid, right? Let's do this.
lines.52: Damn it... It's not just one or two of 'em...! Selgir...!
lines.57: Yes, you can't leave them, can you? Let's go...!
lines.72: --What a surprise. Quite the big catch to call a rat.
lines.93: Just one of the snakes that nest in Kowloon. The vermin lying there are my prey.
lines.97: So I'd like to thank you. Would you join me for a meal, people of Starview Village?
lines.102: Tsangli, the mafia that has grown most powerful in Kowloon in recent years. She's the woman who accomplished that in a single generation.
lines.104: Its rapid growth is also the result of fierce gang wars. I hear many organizations were swallowed by Tsangli... I doubt we ran into her by coincidence.
lines.108: Geez... What does that gorilla soldier want us to do against the mafia?
lines.113: Forgive me. I've kept you waiting.
lines.122: I had my men wait outside. Against the likes of you, they'd be useless and unnecessary, wouldn't they?
lines.125: Let's make a deal, Starview Village. I'm prepared to offer you information on the "Star Augurs", your enemies.
lines.128: If you wish, standing in Kowloon, information, or even ammunition-- I'll provide whatever you need.
lines.132: ...And what do you want from us in return?
lines.136: The wisdom and power of other worlds. So that we, Tsangli, can seize dominance over Kowloon.
lines.144: Then I'll change my demands and my offer. That's what negotiating is for, isn't it?
lines.147: At the very least, I believe we can agree on a mutual non-aggression pact.
lines.151: We don't need information on the Star Augurs. Instead, let us look into the child's whereabouts.
lines.154: Just letting us go over the "transaction" records of the organization we crushed will do. Today, before anything can be covered up.
lines.164: Your face changed. ...Hey. What were you planning to "do" with those kids...?
lines.170: That's enough, both of you. What she's doing is likely the opposite.
lines.178: I looked into Tsangli before, on another matter involving the colonel. It was a routine money-laundering trail, but--
lines.181: Strangely enough, part of the money was going to "child welfare"-- to educational institutions, with no strings attached.
lines.186: The Steel Wolf has sharp eyes.
lines.190: ...So today was about saving kids too...?
lines.195: But that's information that would be a weakness for a mafia boss. A cold-blooded boss has no use for such a thing.
lines.199: ......I'll provide the information. But that girl-- I can't hand over Rin.
lines.204: Why? Even now, her parents are waiting for her to come home--
lines.207: That man is no parent of hers...!
lines.210: On paper, she's probably his "adopted daughter". But Rin was originally a child of Kowloon. ...So I took her back.
lines.214: ...Understood. Then I'll say nothing more. Let's go, Nimbus. Selgir.
lines.218: You believe me awfully easily. Why is that?
lines.222: Even when we pointed our guns at you, you were smiling. But I glimpsed a fire in your eyes.
lines.224: Those are the eyes of someone who knows anger, and love. ...Selgir's story made sense.
lines.235: Won't you take your seats again, people of Starview Village? The food hasn't even come yet.
lines.238: And let's continue our talk. About increasing what I can do to change the future of Kowloon.
lines.243: Haha. Should've just said that from the start.
lines.246: Then bring us some good food. I've got a refined palate, believe it or not, so it'll take more than a little to impress me.
lines.250: Oh, on that point, I have no intention of losing.

2.title: Street-Corner Villain
2.summary: In Shibuya, where rebuilding is underway, Ranmei meets a boy who used to be in Aegis and keeps pushing himself too hard. Torn between a sense of duty from his past deeds and the guilt of finding it painful anyway, the boy is cornered, but Ranmei's drastic treatment saves him.

lines.9: A little more! A little more to the right! I said right! No, too far! Get it together, Flying Prince~!!
lines.13: I always tell you I'm bad at fine control, don't I!?
lines.20: Overflowing with energy. And yet peaceful and calm. How strange.
lines.23: And though its wounds remain, everyone can still work together...
lines.27: Is... that so...? I mean, I do think everyone's working super hard...
lines.31: To you, it's just natural, isn't it. I'm a little envious.
lines.45: Yes. You're receiving from this town something I long for endlessly. That's a wonderful thing.
lines.50: Huh...? Heh? No idea what's going on, but thanks~.
lines.58: You are not fine! You collapsed from overwork! What you need now is rest!
lines.61: ...You're one of the rebuilding volunteers the youth group looks after, aren't you? I heard about it from Mayor Takamori.
lines.63: But why push so hard...? You're only a volunteer, aren't you?
lines.66: 'Cause people like us aren't allowed to say it's hard!!
lines.68: My buddies... the old guy, everyone's working seriously hard. The whole town, together...
lines.71: ...I don't think that's needed, though. That kinda thing...
lines.75: ...I see. It's certainly not all good. And I agree.
lines.78: Hey, are you okay!? I heard you collapsed!?
lines.82: It's fine. It's okay, it's okay. Don't rush. We'll be waiting for you!
lines.84: Once you've rested up and you're feeling better, let's work hard together again!
lines.88: Excuse me, do you have a moment?
lines.92: I'm the one who took care of this boy. And I'd like to discuss something.
lines.105: Your power. Psychic powers, you called it. It's a wonderful power. I could pay a high price for you.
lines.108: H-hey! What are you trying to--
lines.111: You don't have to use your power for the things that bind you.
lines.114: I-- a villain like me-- can forgive your mistakes.
lines.119: Stop it! He's working hard right now! Trying to walk the right path--
lines.122: Even though that "rightness" that says he mustn't call it hard is eating away at him?
lines.128: N-no... old man, it's my fault...!
lines.133: I knew you all had worries. That's exactly why I thought you needed a place to work hard, if you wanted to.
lines.135: But if it's not like that, you can say so! If you want to complain, you can complain as much as you like...!
lines.137: No, I'm the one who made it so you couldn't say it... I'm truly sorry!
lines.142: ...Hehe, too bad. It seems there was no need for a villain.
lines.152: It's the only way I've ever lived.
lines.161: Drastic treatment, you could say... It was an act, to drain the infection.
lines.165: It was no act. I was seriously recruiting him.
lines.168: If the weak, and those who've gone astray, live in a world where all they can do is punish themselves, then that world deserves to be trampled.
lines.171: That's the way I can teach.
lines.177: And yet you want to rebuild society. What a difficult personality.
lines.181: ...But y'know, I kinda get it. Honestly, I was kinda swayed.
lines.184: I mean, we screw up all the time. I don't wanna screw up, but it's impossible, really.
lines.187: So I'm like, can't be helped, right? But he didn't seem like he'd listen. That was super cool, what you did.
lines.194: But the fact that you can say that is also something this town has built up, I'm sure.
lines.198: You can't suddenly start calling something natural when it isn't.
lines.202: Will you show me a bit more of this town? I'd especially like to see the schools and educational facilities.
lines.206: Huh, uh... But I can't really say anything smart...?
lines.213: I'm sure what you felt is what matters.

3.title: The Girl Who Wanted Freedom
3.summary: Ranmei is delighted to hear about a new float planned for construction, but other mafias begin to interfere. Unable to let Tsangli's involvement come to light, Ranmei is at a loss, but Light and the others' scheme makes the float's solid backers clear, blocking the mafias from getting involved.

lines.6: You've come a little too early. You've seen something I'd rather you hadn't.
lines.10: ...I've come to understand that when you say that, it usually means something good happened.
lines.14: That was an eccentric with a taste for charity. He barged in saying he wants to build a new float near Kowloon.
lines.17: He said he'd build an educational institution. A place to take in Kowloon's people, and a road open to the outer floats too.
lines.20: ...Is he a fool, or does he just have nerves of steel? Either way, he's an oddball.
lines.25: It's written all over her face that she's happy...
lines.29: I see. That's good news, then?
lines.34: Who knows. ...I just hope it doesn't turn into a headache.
lines.37: More importantly, the goods you asked for have arrived.
lines.39: I get wisdom, and you get information on the Star Augurs. That's the deal, after all.
lines.42: --It was a good deal, Starview Village. I'd be glad if we could keep up this partnership.
lines.46: Excuse me...! Boss, there's a problem with that matter...!
lines.51: Other organizations are meddling with the new float's construction site?
lines.55: For now, yes. But it doesn't seem to be just a matter of them sniffing out money.
lines.60: Weapons are being brought in. And soldiers are being gathered from outside organizations.
lines.68: No. The new float belongs to outside capital and a philanthropist. Tsangli has no hand in it.
lines.71: ...Or so the story goes. Besides, that place is outside our territory to begin with. It's where the land government keeps watch.
lines.72: The mafia can't possibly move openly there. Something's wrong...
lines.76: ...Perhaps they've caught the scent of your connection.
lines.80: Your outfit got big by fighting gang war after gang war, right? ...Well, you've got no shortage of grudges.
lines.82: Either they've got the land government on board-- or they've lost their minds and stopped caring about that. The second one's a pain.
lines.88: If I move here, my connection to Tsangli will become obvious.
lines.89: And even if I won that fight, that float would fall into the hands of Tsangli-- of the mafia.
lines.93: Then it would be meaningless... It couldn't open up our future...
lines.103: Something, there must be something I can do...
lines.111: We get information. In exchange, we give you wisdom. Wasn't that it?
lines.115: Hey, didn't you forget what you said yourself just now?
lines.125: If that's what you wish. Ranmei.
lines.136: Then let's do this pirate-style. ...Though it looks like we'll need to put on a bit of a show.
lines.140: Hahaha! Fools! Giving us an excuse to attack-- I could cry, I'm so grateful!
lines.143: ...You seem to be having a lot of fun. Esmeralda?
lines.146: Hmph. The Kowloon brats gave me a lot of trouble when I was setting up Bellaqua Casino.
lines.147: Surely I'm allowed a little payback?
lines.151: --The interior has been secured. Only one enemy ship remains.
lines.154: It's a "Tsangli" ship. Watch out for cannon fire.
lines.158: You heard her, Mermaid Pirates. Can you do it?
lines.162: Like, obviously! Easy peasy~. We can totally sink the ship, right?
lines.166: You don't intend to kill a single one of them anyway, do you? Do as you like.
lines.177: And so, mafia gentlemen. From here on, the Mermaid Pirates will be running that new float.
lines.179: We have no intention of encroaching on Kowloon's territory. If possible, we'd like to talk business. Would that be acceptable?
lines.197: Neither the mafias nor those behind them knew it, but the new float had solid backing.
lines.199: Esmeralda, the casino owner of Paradise Isle, and Pern of Miner's Front.
lines.202: And the Mermaid Pirates, self-proclaimed successors of the Crimson Blades. That's how we decided to frame it.
lines.206: ...The Steel Wolf moved first, didn't he? You got me.
lines.211: Tsangli helped its brethren, but lost three ships. Utterly humiliated.
lines.215: Still, even I was surprised that members of the mafias we crushed switched to working for Miner's Front.
lines.219: The outlaws of this city were all outcasts who'd lost their place to begin with. Give them somewhere they're fairly valued, and that's what happens.
lines.222: ...My thanks to you all, once again. Thank you for helping me.
lines.227: So? What are you gonna do now? You're still gonna keep that up?
lines.235: I've gained allies. Next time, I can do even better.
lines.240: Good grief. You never learn, do you...

5000655/1.19:
One of the mafia groups making a name for itself on Kowloon Float.
It has waged countless gang wars, and it's said that its boss Ranmei has swallowed many organizations, and that she has ties to all sorts of groups.
